veranderings.rede: Without a comma 'Net soos ons het die boere' can first be misread as one phrase; the comma after the preposed comparison makes the structure clear.

veranderings.voor: By latere gemeenskappe en vandag nog is
veranderings.na: By latere gemeenskappe, en vandag nog, is
veranderings.rede: 'en vandag nog' is an inserted afterthought between the opening phrase and the verb; enclosing it in commas makes the sentence easier to read.

veranderings.voor: weet goed watter plant om te gebruik
veranderings.na: weet goed watter plant hy of sy moet gebruik
veranderings.rede: 'watter plant om te gebruik' copies the English 'which plant to use'; a full clause with 'moet' is more natural Afrikaans and matches 'Hy of sy' earlier in the block.

veranderings.voor: watter plante om te soek en hoe om hulle te gebruik
veranderings.na: watter plante hulle moes soek en hoe om dit te gebruik
veranderings.rede: 'watter plante om te soek' is the same English pattern, and 'hulle' directly after 'jonger mense' can be read as the people rather than the plants; 'dit' refers clearly to the plants.

vlae.teks: 'n Sangoma gee geestelike leiding. Hy of sy vra die voorouers om leiding.
vlae.rede: 'leiding' is repeated in two consecutive sentences, which reads slightly wooden; the second sentence matches the sangoma glossary entry, so changing either wording risks the definition or the content, and is left for the reviewer or writer to judge.

beskerm_bedenkings.rede: The protected list keeps 'nyanga', but the lesson and its glossary headword use 'inyanga' throughout (the isiZulu form with the noun prefix, beside 'In isiZulu'). Nothing was changed; a person should confirm which spelling is decided, because the protection as written does not match any whole word in the lesson.
